diagnosis: Tool replacement was already active. Missing wood inputs caused local underground acquisition; unlike lighting supply, replacement tools did not first retrace the retained route. Local access then repeatedly selected stone breaks without a tool.
change: Policy v70 shares outward resupply selection between lighting and replacement tools; preserve search, return route, ingredient commitments, and alternative-tool bounds. Directly available recipe inputs avoid outbound travel.
unitProof: New regression failed on v69 because the child was Acquire instead of Resupply; v70 passes outward-route and local-material cases plus existing tool interruption/resumption and bounded alternatives.
limitations: The old tape is incomplete. Only the prefix through the observed failure was replayed exactly.
This does not prove that every future route is passable without a tool or that access handles every missing capability.
New remote-tool scenario awaits live verification.
